evidence.text: The company's FY2026 guide of at least $140m revenue (raised twice, last on 2026-08-04) sits about $7m above the ~$133m street FY consensus. H1 was $62.6m, so the guide needs $77.4m in H2: about $41.6m in Q4 if Q3 prints the $35.8m consensus, against roughly $34.6m implied by the street's FY number. A reaffirmed $140m therefore reads as a Q4 about 20% above where the street sits. A cut to the low $130s only matches what the street already models.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-04): guide raised $130m to $140m and margin to 28%, stock +8.42% (baseline; Simply Wall St cites +23.4% over several days). Q4 2025 (2026-03-04): +18.65%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): revenue beat with guide raised but margin slipped, -27.4%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed the guide, the street FY number would sit at or above $140m, not $133m. And the stock would not be down 32% since the guide was raised, trading below its 200-day average (~$13.4) and near a 12-month low. The price is discounting a guide cut, so a plain reaffirmation is not in it.
evidence.independence: Company guide from the Q2 8-K, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000056/ampx-2026x08x04x8kex991.htm. Same CFO commentary source as the supply finding (allmind call summary), which argues the other way.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue visibility from company documents. On the Q2 call (2026-08-05) the CFO said open POs gave 'good visibility through Q3', with orders received and shipped inside the quarter as in the prior two quarters. Inventory rose $3.3m to $11.5m 'to support the Q3 ramp'. The 10-Q puts remaining performance obligations at $36.5m on 2026-06-30, all due within a year, which by itself roughly matches the $35.8m Q3 consensus. The $24m European drone order ships over about 2.5 quarters from Q2, roughly $9-10m a quarter. Together these point to Q3 revenue at or modestly above the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not reliably paid here. Q1 2026 revenue of $28.5m beat ~$25.3m consensus by 12% and the stock fell 27.4% on margin and EPS. Q2's beat came with a raise and rose 8.4%. Q3 2025 beat ($21.4m vs $17.5m) rose 13.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus of ~5% sequential growth already embeds a modest beat-free Q3. The reported-quarter line sits inside what the company guided, so most of it is priced. What is not obviously priced is that the RPO alone nearly covers the bar. If it were priced, the street would sit at $37-38m rather than $35.8m.
evidence.independence: 10-Q RPO figure from a separate primary document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000059/ampx-20260630.htm. Shares the call-summary source with the guidance and supply findings.

evidence.text: The CFO said on the Q2 call that supply is the main constraint 'particularly in Q4 and into next year'. Capacity is >2 GWh, about 12-15m cells a quarter. The US network has no pouch partner yet, the Fremont pilot line starts only in December 2026 and CAMINUS volume only in Q1 2027. That leaves the Q4 ramp the $140m guide needs, and any 2027 framing, exposed to contract-manufacturer output.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a supply-capped guide. The closest is Q1 2026 (-27.4%), when margin and EPS disappointed despite a revenue beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was said in public on the call, and the street's $133m FY figure may already reflect it. Some of it is not priced: if management quantifies a Q4 cap below the guide, the guide cut becomes explicit. Sized small, and shrunk further for the ~15.6% short interest.
evidence.independence: Same call summary as the guidance finding, read in the opposite direction. Those two are one source and partly offset. Briefglance's preview lists CAMINUS timing as an open risk: https://briefglance.com/articles/amprius-q3-earnings-preview-the-asset-light-gamble-in-next-gen-batteries

evidence.text: On 2026-11-09 China's MOFCOM said it will keep suspending its October 2025 export controls until 2027-01-10. Those controls cover lithium-ion cells of 300 Wh/kg or more, the class SiCore falls in (Announcement 58; suspension under Announcement 70 was due to lapse 2026-11-10). This removes a cliff dated the day of the print. But the relief is only two months, and Amprius' own 10-Q flags these controls as a supply risk for its China contract manufacturers.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it was public on 11-09 and spot is $8.98 against $8.38 on 11-03. What is not priced is management's answer on the call about China-sourced cell supply after 2027-01-10. That could go either way, so it is sized near zero with a positive tilt for the removed immediate cliff.
evidence.independence: 10-Q risk factor: enforcement 'suspended until at least November 2026', https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000059/ampx-20260630.htm. Chinaprospect notes the formal legal notice may lag: https://chinaprospect.com/china-export-controls-rare-earths-battery-materials/

evidence.text: Shipments to Ukraine were $10.4m in Q2 (31% of revenue) and $20.5m in H1 (10-Q), with EMEA at 68%. Since the company last spoke, Ukraine's drone budget came under stress: on 2026-09-25 Zelensky said drones for Jan-Mar must be ordered and paid in Oct-Nov. Then the EU disbursed EUR1.24bn (10-07) and EUR2.86bn (10-14) for Ukrainian-made drones, and Germany said on 10-04 it will fund tens of thousands of interceptor drones. Net, this supports Q4 orders from the largest end market.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately disclosed before. The concentration figure comes from the 10-Q and has not been a headline line on a print.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy that Amprius has not confirmed. The Ukraine share is in the 10-Q but is not in previews or wire copy. If the market had connected the EU drone tranches to Amprius' largest customer region, the drone-battery sell-off into October would not have taken the stock to a 12-month low. Sized small because it is a proxy and one region. The remaining ~69% of revenue (Europe ex-Ukraine, North America, APAC) also has to hold.
evidence.independence: 10-Q (Ukraine $10.4m): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000059/ampx-20260630.htm. Budget stress, the counter-fact: https://kyivindependent.com/zelensky-warns-ukraine-could-face-serious-challenges-with-drones-this-winter-amid-budget-deficit/ (2026-09-25). Germany: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/04/8056450/

evidence.why_not_priced: Amprius made a new 12-month low (~$7.3-7.7) in mid-October, after the Enovix pre-release. evidence.text: Gross margin is the line this stock has sold on. The FY guide of at least 28% needs about 31% in H2 (Earnings Whispers arithmetic) against 27% in Q2, and Q2 was itself up from 20% in Q1. The CFO said H2 margin 'could have upside' but that the guide assumes at least 60% Europe and at least 60% pouch in the mix. A Q3 margin under ~29% would make the FY margin guide look unreachable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: margin fell from 24% to 20% and EPS missed, stock -27.4% despite a 12% revenue beat. Q2 2026: margin rose to 27% with a raise, stock +8.4%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bar is not visible in consensus EPS (-$0.01 is near break-even and could be hit on revenue alone). The 31% H2 requirement is arithmetic that only one preview spelled out. Sign uncertain and the range is wide. Shrunk because the short interest is crowded.
evidence.independence: Company margin guide and Q2 margin from the 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000056/ampx-2026x08x04x8kex991.htm. Same EW preview as the guidance finding.

evidence.text: Amprius filed an S-3ASR automatic universal shelf on 2026-10-09 with no ATM agreement and no selling holders. Its $100m ATM was fully used and terminated in 2025, and none was drawn in 2026. Cash was $74.5m on 2026-06-30 after a $40.1m H1 operating outflow (including the $20m Colorado lease exit), and AR has swelled to $40.7m. A post-print offering is mechanically ready. What the money would buy: Fremont pilot line tools (40% installed), the in-kind share of the ~$100m acCELLerate line conversion (only ~$22m of the $75m DoW award obligated), and contract-manufacturing capacity the CFO says binds supply. Demand is corroborated by orders, the peer print and the guide, so the financing answer is 'funds visible demand': signed zero.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No offering has been announced alongside a print in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The shelf is public but rarely read. An overnight deal after the print, at prices near the 12-month low, would land inside the window. The 10-Q states cash suffices for twelve months, and the use of funds is corroborated, so this is signed at zero with a negative tail in the range.
evidence.independence: 10-Q liquidity and ATM status: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001899287/000189928726000059/ampx-20260630.htm. DoW funding detail: https://dronexl.co/2026/09/30/amprius-75m-drone-battery-grant-unfunded/

evidence.text: No new utility spectrum agreement has been disclosed since 2026-04-21. Anterix files an 8-K item 8.01 for every utility sale, down to the $0.77m Benton PUD deal (8-Ks 2026-02-02, 04-01, 04-06, 04-21). Its only 8.01 since then is the 2026-09-18 buyback. So the fiscal Q2 (Jul-Sep) release very likely reports a second straight quarter with zero new customers, unless a deal signed after September 30 is held for the release. The Earnings Whispers preview says about a dozen opportunities are 'active'.
evidence.source_date: 2026-11-10 (EDGAR 8-K list read on this date; last deal 8-K dated 2026-04-21)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026 print: no new customers signed and a profit beat. The stock fell 3.2% after hours, about 11.5% early the next session, and closed -4.45% (baseline; https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/anterix-shares-fall-despite-first-quarter-earnings-beat-93CH-4852887). Feb 2026 print (CPS deal already announced 2026-02-02): -1.45%. Prints carrying new FCC or deal news went the other way: Jun 2026 +25.72%, Nov 2025 +13.68%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the preview already says 'none were signed last quarter', and the stock is down 11% over 20 days with put skew of +26.6. What is not fully priced is the 6.5-month dry spell, now two full quarters, during a period management called 'accelerating interest'. If it were fully priced, the Aug-style sell-the-print reaction would not recur. A surprise deal announced with the release is the upside tail and is why the range runs positive.
evidence.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/414384/anterix-heads-into-earnings-with-strategic-review-not-revenue-driving-the-debate, 2026-11-03) independently says no new utility customers were signed last quarter. A WebSearch for October 2026 Anterix utility agreements found none.

evidence.text: Insiders sold at $80-85 in the post-Q1 open window, outside any 10b5-1 plan. CEO Scott Lang sold 15,000 shares at $80.00 on 2026-09-21 (10b5-1 box 0), leaving 26,470 direct (about 36% of his direct stake). The Chief Legal Officer sold 4,357 at $85.44 on 2026-09-08 (about 46% of her holdings, not under a plan). A director, Leslie Daniels, sold 2,500 at $83.83 on 2026-09-10 (not under a plan). The CFO also sold about 5,000 on 2026-10-09, but under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-22. Discretionary sales cleared by the general counsel are hard to square with a strategic transaction being near as of September, so a deal announcement alongside this print is less likely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on insider sales. The strategic review has run since February 2025 with no outcome across six prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: finviz shows insider transactions at -36.82% and lists the CEO sale, and a Seeking Alpha piece is titled 'the chart and the insiders say wait'. What may not be priced is the inference, not the fact: a non-plan sale by the CEO and the CLO implies the review held no MNPI in September. If the market had fully absorbed that, the stock would carry no deal premium into the print, and it still trades at about $1.48bn against $116m of cash.
evidence.independence: Same insider set seen across three separate Form 4s (CLO https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1304492/000166994326000019/0001669943-26-000019.txt filed 2026-09-08; director https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1304492/000105255926000006/0001052559-26-000006.txt filed 2026-09-11). evidence.text: On 2026-09-16 the board approved a new $250m buyback, effective 2026-09-22 through 2029-09-22, replacing the expiring $226.7m program. The company made no repurchases in fiscal Q1 (Q1 10-Q). The 2026-11-03 Earnings Whispers preview still tells investors to 'look for an update' on the expiring authorisation, so at least one widely read preview missed the renewal. Any repurchases from late September onward, or an execution plan, would show in the Q2 10-Q Part II Item 2 or on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print turned on buyback execution. The prior $226.7m program sat unused in Q1 FY27.
evidence.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public in an 8-K, but the Earnings Whispers preview written six weeks later does not know about it. Authorisations at this company have historically gone unused. Actual purchases at $75-85 by a company with $116m of cash and no debt would be new information. If buying were priced, the -11% 20-day drawdown would be harder to explain. A $250m program against a $1.48bn cap is about 17% of the shares. Execution is uncertain: insiders were selling at the same time, and management has said it may need to raise capital.
evidence.independence: Q1 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1304492/000130449226000046/atex-20260630.htm, 2026-08-11) confirms no repurchases in Q1, $226.7m remaining, $116.0m cash, no debt.

evidence.text: Syndax's Q3 2026 release and call (2026-11-02), the only other approved menin inhibitor, put Revuforj new patients at about 300 (+20% QoQ) with about 50% NPM1, so about 150 NPM1 new starts. Management claimed 'dominant share of all patients starting a menin inhibitor' and more than 80% of class revenue. Against this, Kura's Q2 'majority share of NPM1 menin new starts' rested on about 115 starts. Unless KOMZIFTI Q3 starts exceed about 150 (+30% QoQ), that claim is unlikely to be repeated, and the market will hear it on the call while bleximenib is already the overhang.

The finding is on starts and share commentary, not the revenue line, and is sized net of that.

The preview frames a backlog meaningfully above $111M as the test. After quarter end came another $6.3M (10-13, taking that customer above $19M since July 1, double its whole FY26) and an order of undisclosed value for more than 50,000 drone optical assemblies (10-27).

Q2 FY26 (2026-02-11) rose 21.5%. Backlog stalling was the cited cause of the September drop (https://finviz.com/news/415717/lightpaths-july-production-orders-face-first-test-as-backlog-stall-weighs-on-shares).
evidence.why_not_priced: The orders are public, but the stock is down ~17% since the last print and 13% over 20 days, so it is priced as though the backlog stall continues. If the market believed backlog would grow again, the stock would not sit near the 52-week-low band, 45% below the June $14 offering, with ~$93M of June-30 cash against a ~$540M market cap. The deconsolidation of China backlog and delivery stretching to CY2027 can hide the growth, which is why this is not sized larger.
